items.title: Seeder inserts exactly the four seeded promotions
covers: AC: seed data matches the table
items.reason: The seed table has per-row requirements (rule type, coupon-only, status, window); a single case asserts each row so a wrong type or window fails with a precise diff.

items.title: Seeder inserts coupons FALL10 and WELCOME5 on the coupon-only promotion
items.reason: Later stories (PROMO-4) rely on these codes belonging to the coupon-only promotion; separate from the promotion rows because it exercises the foreign key and the empty redemption table.

items.title: Restarting against the same database keeps 4 promotions and 2 coupons
covers: AC: starts again against the same database
items.reason: Aspire restarts the service routinely; a seeder that appended on every start would duplicate promotions and double-count them in `/active`.

items.title: Seeder inserts nothing when Promotions already has a row
covers: Outputs: if the Promotions table already has any row, the seeder inserts nothing
items.reason: Distinct from a plain restart: here the existing row is not seed data, so it proves the guard checks any row, not a count of 4.

items.title: /health and /alive return 200 when the database is reachable
items.reason: Aspire's health check and readiness depend on these endpoints; checked at the functional layer because it needs the real service and database.

items.title: GET /active returns the four seeded promotions and no inactive ones
covers: Outputs: coupon-only promotions count as active
items.reason: Core filter rule: Published and inside the window. The three extras each break one condition (status, end, start), so a filter that drops any one condition fails here.

items.title: GET /active orders promotions by priority descending
items.reason: Order is part of the contract that PROMO-3 consumes; split from the filter case so an ordering bug does not hide behind a membership assertion.

items.title: Promotions with equal priority are ordered by id ascending
items.reason: The seeded priorities are all distinct, so the tie-break needs its own data; without it the order is nondeterministic across runs.

items.title: Each active promotion has the required fields
covers: Outputs: each element has id, name, type, status, startsAt, endsAt, priority, requiresCoupon
items.reason: PROMO-2 owns the final shape, but the story fixes this minimum; checking values rather than presence catches a type/status serialized as a number.

items.title: GET /active returns 200 and an empty array when nothing is active
covers: Outputs: when no promotion is active it returns 200 with []
items.reason: An empty result must not be 404 or null; callers iterate the body.

items.title: A promotion with StartsAt equal to now is active
items.reason: Lower boundary of the window; an off-by-one (`<`) would hide a promotion at the instant it starts. Uses a fake `TimeProvider` so the instant is exact.

items.title: A promotion with EndsAt equal to now is not active
items.reason: Upper boundary is exclusive; an off-by-one (`<=`) would keep applying a promotion after it ended. Uses a fake `TimeProvider`.

items.title: GET /active ignores a malformed bearer token
covers: Outputs: ignores any bearer token sent with it
AC: malformed bearer token still returns 200
items.reason: Anonymous endpoints can still fail with 401 when the auth middleware validates a bad token first; this protects anonymous callers whose client sends a stale header.

items.title: GET /active returns the same result with a valid token
covers: Outputs: ignores any bearer token sent with it
items.reason: Confirms a valid token neither changes the result nor causes per-user filtering.

items.title: GET /api/promotions with a promotions-scope token returns every promotion
covers: Outputs: GET /api/promotions returns 200 with every promotion, active or not
items.reason: Distinguishes the admin-style list from `/active`: inactive rows must be included. Functional layer because the token is validated against a real Identity.

items.title: Signing in to the WebApp yields a token with the promotions scope that is accepted

items.reason: Only the real WebApp sign-in proves the WebApp requests the scope and the webapp client is allowed it; no cheaper layer exercises both sides. Test stack scenario must load promotions data because the stack runs with `Seeding__Disabled=true`.

items.title: GET /api/promotions with a malformed token returns 401
items.reason: A garbage token must be rejected, not treated as anonymous; separate from the missing-token case because the validation path differs.

items.title: GET /api/promotions with an expired token returns 401
items.reason: Lifetime validation is a separate failure from format validation.

Reshape PROMO-1's Promotion/PromotionTarget to the contract (Scope All|Brand|Type|Product, nullable TargetId, Value, MinOrderTotal, Description, IsStackable, Status Ended replacing Archived) in one migration; leave Coupon/CouponRedemption tables as they are (PROMO-4 reshapes them). Rewrite the seeder to PROMO-3's data: 'Fall Hiking Sale' PercentOff 20 on Type 3 (priority 10), BuyXGetY 2+1 on Product 40, AmountOffOrder $10 with MinOrderTotal 150 on All, and the coupon-only PercentOff with coupons FALL10/WELCOME5, all Published with the PROMO-1 windows. Badge label computed per contract. Lifecycle worker runs every 30s (TimeProvider + PeriodicTimer), records StartedEventSentAt/EndedEventSentAt, publishes via the IntegrationEventLogEF outbox; /end publishes Ended at once.…

Decisions: /evaluate requires authentication; BuyXGetY is non-stackable only. PricingEngine is pure (no DB, no clock) so PROMO-5 and QE can trust one implementation. Candidates come from PROMO-2's ActivePromotionsQuery through a 30s PromotionCache (key 'active-promotions', make it tenant-ready by keeping the key in one place). Define ICouponValidator/CouponCheck exactly as the contract and register NotProvidedCouponValidator; a coupon-only promotion applies only when the check returns Applied for its PromotionId. Do not touch the Coupon tables. Uses PROMO-2's Promotion.BadgeLabel. If tests/Promotions.UnitTests does not exist, QE creates it; only add it to the solution filter if you create it.

Decisions: AppliedPromotionIds as a Postgres integer[] column on Orders; Promotions.API down or slow (2s) -> accept client discounts after the bounds check and log. Add the optional catalogTypeId/catalogBrandId to Ordering's BasketItem (contract) so the re-check can build an /evaluate request; lines without them are not re-checked (deviation from the story, record it). Bounds check returns 400 in CreateOrderAsync before the command; Order.GetTotal() subtracts discounts and the summary SQL query does the same. Add CouponCode/TotalDiscount to Ordering's OrderStatusChangedToPaidIntegrationEvent only (subscribers own their own copies). IPromotionsClient forwards the buyer token; /evaluate has no side effects so re-checking never burns coupons. Do not touch WebApp.

Reshape Coupon/CouponRedemption to the contract in one migration (seeded FALL10/WELCOME5 survive, upper-case). CouponValidator implements PROMO-3's ICouponValidator unchanged and replaces the NotProvided registration; /coupons/{code}/validate uses the same validator. Expired covers coupon ExpiresAt, promotion EffectiveStatus != Active and a deleted coupon. Declare Promotions.API's own OrderStatusChangedToPaidIntegrationEvent copy with OrderId, BuyerIdentityGuid, CouponCode, TotalDiscount (PROMO-5's shape); idempotent on unique OrderId; over-redemption saved with IsOverRedemption + warning. Publish CouponRedeemedIntegrationEvent through PROMO-2's outbox service. Admin endpoints use PromotionsPolicies.Admin. Bulk code generation is out of scope (follow-up). Update promo-1 scenario SQL to the new coupon schema.

Owns WebApp PromotionsService (GetActivePromotionsAsync + 60s IMemoryCache + InvalidateActive) and its registration; PROMO-8 later adds EvaluateAsync to the same class. Badge component is parameter-only (no services) so HybridApp can reuse it. 'Shop the sale' links to the existing filtered catalog URL (type or brand query), no new /sale page. WebApp keeps its own copies of PromotionStarted/Ended events; both handlers call InvalidateActive. Countdown in plain browser JS modelled on chat-fab.js; HeaderBar stays static SSR. Use PromotionPricing.SalePrice (ToEven rounding) so the display price equals PROMO-3's quantity-1 result. Never call /evaluate from the catalog.

Stretch. Page /admin/copilot with [Authorize(Policy="Admin")] from the foundation (403 for non-admins). Separate PromotionsAdminService typed client with AddAuthToken for the PROMO-2 admin and PROMO-4 coupon APIs; reuse WebAppComponents CatalogService (semantic search, GetTypes, GetBrands) and do not edit it; fall back to name search when semantic search fails. Tool GetCurrentDate uses TimeProvider. Never call /publish from a tool, only from the Publish button; 'make it 25%' updates the same draft via PUT. Show 'AI isn't configured' when no IChatClient is registered. No audit table (Aspire traces suffice).

Extend PROMO-6's PromotionsService with EvaluateAsync (authenticated, 2s, null on failure); do not create a second promotions client. BasketState calls /evaluate once per cached basket, builds BasketPricing and sends items[].discount, catalogTypeId, catalogBrandId, appliedPromotionIds and couponCode (only when Applied) per PROMO-5's contract. Coupon comes from IAppliedCouponStore; ship NullAppliedCouponStore and leave cookie persistence and the coupon UI to PROMO-9. Put the summary box in CartSummary.razor. Reason->message mapping is a static CouponMessages helper; MinOrderNotMet uses nextThreshold. Clear the cookie in CheckoutAsync after a successful order. covers: Outputs: banner - highest priority promotion that targets All, Type or Brand
items.reason: The banner rule filters by target scope. A Product-only promotion with the highest priority must not take the banner, otherwise the 'Shop the sale' link has no category to open.

items.title: PromotionEndedIntegrationEvent removes the badge and banner on every later page load
covers: AC: when the WebApp receives PromotionEndedIntegrationEvent the next page load (and every one after it) shows no badge or banner for that promotion
items.reason: The 60s cache would keep the promotion on screen after it ends; only the event handler clears it earlier. The case warms the cache first so a pass cannot come from an empty cache, and polls for less than the 60s cache lifetime.

items.title: PromotionStartedIntegrationEvent makes a newly published promotion visible
items.reason: The started handler is the other cache clear. Promotion 5 is a Draft whose window is already open, so publishing it fires the started event; its `-5%` badge must appear well before the 60s cache expiry.

items.title: With no active promotions every page renders as today
covers: Outputs: Anywhere - no change when there are no active promotions
items.reason: The `default` scenario leaves promotionsdb empty, so `/active` returns `[]`. This is the baseline for the storefront and proves badge, row and banner are all conditional.

items.title: Pages render at normal prices with a warning logged when Promotions.API is down
covers: AC: when Promotions.API can't be reached pages render at normal prices with no badges or banner and a warning is logged
Outputs: Anywhere - no change when Promotions.API is down
items.reason: The storefront must never fail because an optional service is down. A real container stop is the only way to see the WebApp's HttpClient fail the way it does in production.

items.title: A hanging Promotions.API delays a page load by at most the 2s timeout
covers: AC: page load time isn't affected by more than the 2s HttpClient timeout
items.reason: Down is not the same as slow: a paused container accepts connections but never answers, which is the case the 2s timeout exists for. The bound is measured against a baseline load of the same page.

items.title: A coupon-only promotion is never shown on the storefront
covers: AC: promotion with requiresCoupon = true is never shown on the storefront
items.reason: Promotions.API already leaves coupon-only promotions out of `/active`, so a plain run would pass even if the WebApp ignored the flag. Raising promotion 4's priority above all others makes any leak visible as the banner and as a `-10%` badge on every item.

items.title: SalePrice returns round(price x (1 - value/100), 2) for percent offers
covers: Display price rule: round(price x (1 - value/100), 2)
Rule: must match PROMO-3 for a quantity-1 line
items.reason: The display rule is pure arithmetic in `PromotionPricing.SalePrice`; a unit case checks the exact values the e2e tiles rely on, including a value with a third decimal that must be rounded.

items.title: SalePrice with value 100 returns 0.00
covers: Display price rule: round(price x (1 - value/100), 2) at the upper limit of PercentOff value (PROMO-2: 0 < v <= 100)
items.reason: PROMO-2 accepts a value of 100, so the display price boundary must be exact and never negative.

items.title: A promotion matches an item only through the column its target scope names
covers: Inputs: Each CatalogItem (Id, CatalogTypeId, CatalogBrandId) matched against targets
items.reason: Type, Brand and Product targets all carry a numeric id, so mixing up the columns would match the wrong items; the case uses an item whose type id, brand id and own id are all different.

items.title: BestMatch picks the highest priority and breaks ties by the lowest id
covers: Decision: ties go to the lowest id, same order as /active
items.reason: Both the catalog tile and the item page depend on this single ordering; equal priorities cannot be produced reliably through the API stack, so it is a unit case.

items.title: BestMatch ignores a coupon-only promotion even when it has the highest priority
covers: AC: promotion with requiresCoupon = true is never shown (BestMatch)
items.reason: Defense in depth: the story forbids showing coupon-only promotions even if `/active` ever returned one, and this check lives in the shared WebAppComponents code.

items.title: PromotionsService drops coupon-only promotions from the /active response
covers: AC: promotion with requiresCoupon = true is never shown (PromotionsService read)
items.reason: The service is the first of three filters; a fake `HttpMessageHandler` and an in-memory cache make this runnable without services.
